question: Does v58 remove the mid-height line?
hypothesis: The mid-height line on v53–v56 comes from the upper-edge join starting at the widest point (66 mm); v58 has no join that starts partway up.
prediction: The v56 strip shows a line at about 66 mm (6 mm above the strip's base); the v58 strip shows none.
why_this_test: The line appears from v53, when the join began at mid-height, and stays while that join is kept; v51 (no such join) had none. A 40 mm strip across that height answers it in about an hour instead of a 3–4 hour pair.

controlled.settings: v55 0.4 process and filament (from the v57 0.4 project)
controlled.strip: Z 60–72 mm of the 6" pair (PR-002); the line is expected 6 mm above the strip's base

dependent_adjustments.nozzle_variant: Both strips are cut from the 0.6-variant files (the 0.4 v58 files weren't downloaded); both print on the 0.4 so only the model differs.
dependent_adjustments.placement: Two strips on one plate, 25 mm apart, so they share every layer's conditions.

print_runs.note: Taller than the question needs: Z 72–100 belongs to the upper-edge ripple, a separate experiment.

reading.v56: Soft horizontal bands across the face, the strongest near mid-strip; the inner back wall shows a seam line where the two tiles join (z 66). The face line is not clearly stronger than v58's.
reading.v58: The same soft banding on the face. The tiles stay separate; four breakaway ties between the backs leave strings and small raised marks on the back faces (not the show face).

result.answer: v58 is better (owner). Whether the mid-height line itself is gone is still open: the AI reading saw similar soft banding on both faces.
result.owner_words: the ribbed back looks better than the v56 for sure

print_runs.note: Fallback with 10 mm above the line, if 6 mm proves too little to judge.

findings.why: Without these baseline conditions the print's result is graded F.
findings.fix: Dry the filament, run the printer's vibration calibration, confirm the nozzle and plate, and record them.
